scope: Attempted shared finite-cutter Split integration; route was disabled after regressions and is not active in production.
findings: The proposed single-mesh route exposes an exact-contact collision for JSON-number coordinates when a cutter is coplanar with one source face and crosses its neighboring face.

The contact collector records the shared edge twice from the same cutter. The coplanar face supplies approximate parameters without exact provenance; the adjacent face supplies exact cutter-edge witnesses in reverse edge order. Their parameters differ by binary rounding while both produce the same rounded point. The merger rejects an exact contact paired with an unverified one; blindly merging would risk hiding a real collapsed interval.

The attempted route also changed established separate-segment publication expectations. Native static evidence suggests source-mesh replacement, but direct native validation and the published contract remain unresolved.
verification: The temporary route produced six failures in the guarded five-file integration run, including the pre-existing legacy finite-interior test and the new JSON-number precision error. The temporary production route was removed. The restored path and candidate controls passed 117 tests with two explicit expected failures under m2-single-route-disabled-20261028-r1.json. The temporary diagnostic test was removed; collector data remain in m2-edge-debug.json.
next: Prove exact coplanar cutter-edge/source-edge contact identity across neighboring faces before routing the candidate; retain rejection of distinct contacts that round to one coordinate.
limitations: The shared production route still has the finite-interior seam defect.
Native Split output, real worker, rendered GUI and public MCP for the candidate remain unverified.
